findings.obligation: nw-code-craftsmanship semantic DRY and single source of truth: one fact has one owner
findings.observation: Low, non-blocking, quality axis Maintainable (semantic DRY). TeamMetricsReadsParityOnBothProvidersTests.cs and PortfolioMetricsReadsParityOnBothProvidersTests.cs repeat the same support code verbatim: DescribeFeatures (for example "$"portfolios {Loaded(entry.Collection(f => f.Portfolios).IsLoaded)} ..."), SimulationOf, Loaded, AddForecasts, AConnection, BuildProvider and StopPostgres. One fact (how a loaded Feature graph is described for comparison) has two owners, so a change to the Feature graph must be made twice or the two classes silently diverge.
findings.remediation: Extract the shared Feature-graph description, forecast seeding, provider set-up and Postgres teardown into one support type in TestHelpers that both parity classes call. Do not change the comparisons or expected values. Optional, may follow the Story.

findings.obligation: Design: one private helper per repository holds the shared include
findings.observation: Low, non-blocking. WorkItemRepository.cs: the GetAllByPredicate override still spells its own include, "var features = Context.WorkItems\n .Include(wi => wi.Team)\n .Where(predicate);", while the five new reads share the private helper ItemsWithTeam that holds the same Include(Team). The Design said one private helper holds the include; the override is a second owner of that include. Consequence: the parity tests compare the named reads against this override, so if one is edited without the other the comparison would still pass or fail for the wrong reason. The override leaves with S05g, so this is a transient duplicate.
findings.remediation: Make the GetAllByPredicate override return ItemsWithTeam(predicate), or leave it and let S05g delete it. Optional.
